questions.prompt: How does Lugavere frame the course's practical aim?
choices: A Deepest possible PhD-level biochemistry only.
B Actionable nutrition and lifestyle for performance, health, and longevity—not only weed-deep science.
C Calorie-counting apps as the sole curriculum.
D Outsourcing all food decisions to specialists forever.
questions.explain: He prioritizes practical harnessing of nutrition and lifestyle over a pure deep-dive academic tour.

questions.prompt: His working definition of nutrition emphasizes:
choices: A Only social-media trends.
B Providing or obtaining the food necessary for health and growth.
C Fashion and packaging design.
D Eliminating all pleasure from eating.
questions.explain: Nutrition is obtaining food necessary for health and growth.

questions.prompt: Regarding essential nutrients, he notes especially that:
choices: A Carbohydrate is an essential nutrient class humans must eat or die of deficiency disease.
B Essential means we need them to survive (deficiency disease otherwise); there is no essential carbohydrate.
C Only fiber is essential.
D No fats are ever essential.
questions.explain: Essential = needed to avoid deficiency disease; there is no essential carbohydrate.

questions.prompt: Chemically, saturated vs unsaturated fat differs by:
choices: A Color of the food only.
B Saturated fats have no double bonds; unsaturated have one or more double bonds.
C Unsaturated fats never exist in nature.
D Saturated always means industrial trans fat.
questions.explain: No double bonds = saturated; double bond(s) = unsaturated (mono or poly).

questions.prompt: Beyond calories, food is described as information because:
choices: A It has no biological effect.
B It has epigenetic capacity—can change gene expression—and relates to chronic disease and body composition.
C Only supplements count as information.
D Food never affects performance.
questions.explain: Food can change gene expression (epigenetic capacity).
